concept.name: Mass index
concept.definition: Donald Dorsey's volatility indicator: a 25-period sum of the ratio of a 9-period EMA of the high-low range to a double-smoothed 9-period EMA of that range, designed to spot 'reversal bulges' when the daily range expands abnormally.
concept.intuition: When the range EMA swells relative to its own smoothing, the sum bulges - Dorsey's warning that the current trend may be about to reverse.
concept.mechanics: Single = EMA(High - Low, 9); Double = EMA(Single, 9); Mass Index = 25-period sum of (Single / Double). Dorsey's signal is a move above 27 followed by a fall back below 26.5 (the 'reversal bulge'); the indicator is directionless - trade direction comes from the prior trend, and Dorsey paired it with TRIX for timing.
concept.formula: MI = sum over 25 periods of [EMA(H - L, 9) / EMA(EMA(H - L, 9), 9)].
concept.failure_modes: Readings above 27 are rare, so signals are few; thresholds need per-security calibration, and the bulge warns of reversal without saying when or confirming direction.
concept.misconceptions: It is not directional - a bulge after an uptrend warns of a downside reversal and vice versa, and it must be paired with a directional tool.
concept.example: If the EMA ratio runs at 1.04 for 25 straight periods, the Mass Index = 26.0; a push to 27.2 followed by a drop through 26.5 completes a reversal bulge.
